page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.2-8 is an arm64 compute instance utilizing Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. The virtual machine is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores, operating with a single thread per core and no hyperthreading. System memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration guarantees fully dedicated CPU compute slices without resource sharing across neighboring host tenants.

The instance contains no bundled local storage, meaning that all persistent disk storage must be configured via network-attached cloud block volumes. Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct ingress and egress routing. Workloads requiring sustained high input and output disk operations must factor in network transport overhead for all filesystem tasks due to the lack of on-chassis NVMe or SATA devices.

With a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per dedicated core, the server optimizes resource density for execution pipelines that do not demand large in-memory footprints. The single-threaded core model ensures deterministic CPU cycle availability, mitigating latency spikes often observed in multithreaded architectures. However, the absence of x86 vector extensions and onboard storage represents a deliberate architectural tradeoff aimed at straightforward compute efficiency.

This hardware configuration is suited for containerized microservices, distributed web server pools, API backends, code compilation, and continuous integration pipelines. Organizations running modern Arm-native runtimes can deploy scale-out stateless services that benefit from dedicated physical cores while avoiding unnecessary overhead from unutilized memory or local storage.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.2-8 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured for compute-oriented workloads requiring dedicated processing resources. The server utilizes the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family on the arm64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for all persistent data operations and operating system drives. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware delivers single-threaded dedicated cores, each virtual core eliminates noisy-neighbor CPU contention. This lean memory footprint provides an efficient resource balance for processing-centric environments. Workload profiles that align with this instance include distributed web serving, continuous integration and build nodes, microservices orchestration, and lightweight application processing tasks.
